Puerto Rico has no AI-specific legislation on record as of August 2026, making it one of the jurisdictions where the regulatory environment is defined entirely by absence.

That absence has a practical meaning. A territory with no AI bills introduced, passed, or pending places no locally enacted compliance burden on compute infrastructure sited there. For developers choosing where to build data centers, the legislative column is blank, which removes one category of jurisdictional risk, though it says nothing about federal oversight, tax treatment, land availability, or grid capacity.

The data covers only legislative activity and does not extend to executive orders, agency guidance, or federal rules that apply to Puerto Rico as a territory. It also does not capture whether bills were considered and died before introduction, or whether activity has accelerated since the recorded date. The record here is narrow: zero bills, one jurisdiction, one point in time.
